summary: Phase 2 of a 6-phase procurement spend cube system. Builds the supplier harmonisation pipeline on top of the Phase 1 foundation. Implements: (1) name normaliser (suffix stripping, abbreviation expansion, T/A stripping), (2) deterministic matcher (exact normalised name, exact vendor ID), (3) fuzzy matcher (rapidfuzz composite scoring with corroboration signals), (4) embedding similarity matcher (sentence-transformers), (5) LLM parent company enrichment (dry-run aware, batched), (6) supplier master table builder, (7) harmoniser orchestrator tying all stages together. Validation gate: the 10-row sample data correctly merges Acme x3 and Sodexo x2 into canonical suppliers. 10+ passing unit tests.

decisions.pipeline_stages: 5-stage pipeline runs in strict order: normalise → deterministic → fuzzy → embedding → LLM. Each stage only processes suppliers not resolved by earlier stages.
decisions.canonical_supplier_id: Generated as a stable hash of the normalised canonical name (SHA256 first 12 chars) so IDs are reproducible across runs — not random UUIDs.
decisions.fuzzy_composite_score: Weighted average of token_sort_ratio (40%), token_set_ratio (40%), partial_ratio (20%) from rapidfuzz. Corroboration signals (city, postcode, ABN, vendor_id) added as flat point boosts before thresholding.
decisions.embedding_model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via sentence-transformers. Encode normalised supplier names only (not raw). Embeddings cached to disk (data/cache/supplier_embeddings.pkl) to avoid recomputation.
decisions.llm_parent_enrichment: Only runs when config.llm.dry_run = false. Batches 20 canonical suppliers per call. Results always go to review queue (never auto-accepted) — confidence capped at 0.50.
decisions.review_queue: Items with supplier_match_confidence < 0.60 (config.categorisation.confidence_medium) go to review queue. Stored in supplier_match_log with review_status=PENDING.
decisions.idempotency: Running harmoniser twice on same input: checks if canonical_supplier_id already exists in supplier_master before inserting. Updates match_log entries rather than duplicating.
decisions.phase1_foundation: Phase 1 is complete. supplier_master_table and supplier_match_log_table already defined in src/models/database.py. SupplierMaster and SupplierMatchLog pydantic models in src/models/schema.py. legal_suffixes.yaml and abbreviation_map.yaml in data/reference/.

existing_tables.supplier_master: canonical_supplier_id (TEXT PK), canonical_name, parent_company_id, parent_name, country, identifiers (JSON TEXT), created_at, updated_at — defined in src/models/database.py
existing_tables.supplier_match_log: id (TEXT PK), raw_supplier_name, raw_supplier_id, canonical_supplier_id, match_method, confidence (FLOAT), evidence (TEXT), review_status, created_at — defined in src/models/database.py
existing_tables.transactions: All canonical fields including canonical_supplier_id, canonical_supplier_name, parent_company_id, parent_company_name, supplier_match_confidence, supplier_match_method — these get populated by the harmoniser

userStories.title: Implement supplier name normaliser
userStories.description: Implement src/suppliers/normaliser.py. This is Stage 1 of the harmonisation pipeline — always runs first, on every supplier name. It produces a normalised form used for all downstream matching. Must correctly normalise all Acme and Sodexo variants from the sample data into the same normalised string.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/suppliers/normaliser.py — implement SupplierNormaliser class
__init__(self, suffixes_path: str, abbreviations_path: str): loads data/reference/legal_suffixes.yaml and data/reference/abbreviation_map.yaml

Implement normalise(self, name: str) -> str performing in order: (1) return empty string if name is None/blank, (2) lowercase, (3) strip leading/trailing whitespace, (4) remove T/A, T.A., Trading As, t/a prefixes (regex), (5) strip legal entity suffixes from suffix list (word-boundary match, longest first), (6) expand abbreviations from abbreviation map (whole-word match only), (7) remove punctuation except hyphens within words, (8) collapse multiple spaces to single space, (9) strip again

Verify normalise() results: normalise('Acme Pty Ltd') == 'acme', normalise('ACME PTY LIMITED') == 'acme', normalise('acme p/l') == 'acme', normalise('SODEXO AUSTRALIA') == 'sodexo australia', normalise('Sodexo Aust P/L') == 'sodexo australia', normalise('DHL EXPRESS') == 'dhl express', normalise('Telstra Corporation') == 'telstra', normalise('INTERCOMPANY - LEGAL') == 'intercompany legal', normalise(None) == '', normalise('') == ''
Implement normalise_series(self, series: pd.Series) -> pd.Series for vectorised batch normalisation
CLI: python src/suppliers/normaliser.py — runs normalise() on all 10 sample supplier names, prints raw → normalised pairs
Run: python src/suppliers/normaliser.py — exits 0, Acme x3 all normalise to 'acme', Sodexo x2 both normalise to 'sodexo australia'

userStories.title: Implement deterministic supplier matcher
userStories.description: Implement src/suppliers/matcher.py Stage 2: deterministic matching on exact normalised name, exact vendor ID (raw_supplier_id), and cross-system vendor number mapping. This handles the clear-cut cases before fuzzy matching is invoked. Also implements Stage 3 fuzzy matching using rapidfuzz with composite scoring and corroboration signal boosts.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/suppliers/matcher.py — implement DeterministicMatcher class and FuzzyMatcher class
DeterministicMatcher.__init__(self, supplier_master_df: pd.DataFrame): accepts existing supplier master as DataFrame for lookup

DeterministicMatcher.match(self, raw_name: str, normalised_name: str, raw_supplier_id: str = None) -> tuple[str | None, float, str]: returns (canonical_supplier_id, confidence, method). Tries: (1) exact normalised name match → confidence 0.95, method='EXACT_NAME'; (2) exact raw_supplier_id match → confidence 0.99, method='EXACT_VENDOR_ID'. Returns (None, 0.0, '') if no match.
FuzzyMatcher.__init__(self, supplier_master_df: pd.DataFrame, config): stores thresholds from config.supplier_matching

FuzzyMatcher.score(self, name_a: str, name_b: str) -> float: compute weighted composite: token_sort_ratio * 0.40 + token_set_ratio * 0.40 + partial_ratio * 0.20 (all from rapidfuzz, divided by 100 to get 0-1 scale)

FuzzyMatcher.match(self, normalised_name: str, corroboration: dict = None) -> tuple[str | None, float, str, str]: returns (canonical_supplier_id, confidence, method, evidence). Scores against all entries in supplier_master_df. Best score: if raw_score >= auto_threshold/100 → confidence = raw_score/100 * 0.95, method='FUZZY_AUTO'; if raw_score >= review_threshold/100 → confidence = raw_score/100 * 0.85, method='FUZZY_REVIEW'; else (None, raw_score/100, 'FUZZY_REJECT', evidence). Apply corroboration boosts (same_city, same_postcode, same_abn from config) as additive points to raw_score before threshold check.
Both classes return evidence string describing match: e.g. 'token_sort=95 token_set=97 partial=88 composite=0.92 + city_match+5'
CLI: python src/suppliers/matcher.py — tests matching logic on sample supplier variants, prints match results with confidence and method

userStories.title: Implement embedding-based supplier matcher
userStories.description: Implement src/suppliers/embeddings.py Stage 4: sentence-transformer embedding similarity matching for suppliers not resolved by deterministic or fuzzy matching. Caches embeddings to disk to avoid recomputation on repeated runs.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/suppliers/embeddings.py — implement EmbeddingMatcher class
__init__(self, model_name: str = 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2', cache_path: str = 'data/cache/supplier_embeddings.pkl'): loads sentence-transformers model, creates data/cache/ directory if needed
Implement encode(self, names: list[str]) -> np.ndarray: encodes list of normalised names. Checks cache first (dict keyed by name). Encodes uncached names in batch, updates cache, saves cache to disk.

Implement match(self, query_name: str, candidate_names: list[str], candidate_ids: list[str], config) -> tuple[str | None, float, str, str]: encodes query_name, computes cosine similarity against all candidate_names embeddings. Returns (canonical_supplier_id, confidence, method, evidence) where: if top_similarity >= embedding_auto_threshold → confidence = top_similarity * 0.95, method='EMBEDDING_AUTO'; if top_similarity >= embedding_review_threshold → confidence = top_similarity * 0.85, method='EMBEDDING_REVIEW'; else (None, top_similarity, 'EMBEDDING_REJECT', evidence). evidence = f'cosine_similarity={top_similarity:.3f} matched={best_candidate}'
Implement match_batch(self, query_names: list[str], candidate_names: list[str], candidate_ids: list[str], config) -> list[tuple]: batch version for efficiency
If sentence-transformers not available (ImportError): log warning and return (None, 0.0, 'EMBEDDING_UNAVAILABLE', 'sentence-transformers not installed') — do not crash
CLI: python src/suppliers/embeddings.py — encodes sample supplier names, prints similarity matrix for Acme variants

userStories.title: Implement LLM parent company enrichment
userStories.description: Implement src/suppliers/parent_mapper.py Stage 5: LLM-based parent company identification for canonical suppliers where parent is unknown. Must respect dry_run config, batch 20 suppliers per call, and cap all results at LOW confidence (0.50) since LLM results always require human review.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/suppliers/parent_mapper.py — implement ParentMapper class
__init__(self, config): loads config, initialises anthropic.Anthropic() client only if not dry_run

Implement enrich(self, supplier_names: list[str]) -> list[dict]: if config.llm.dry_run is True, log 'DRY RUN: skipping parent company LLM enrichment' and return list of dicts with parent_company_name=None, confidence=0.0, method='DRY_RUN' for each supplier

When not dry_run: batch supplier_names into groups of config.llm.batch_size (default 20). For each batch, send a single Claude API call with prompt: 'For each of the following supplier names, identify the ultimate parent company or corporate group if known. If unsure, return null. Format: JSON array of objects with fields: supplier_name, parent_company_name (null if unknown or same entity), confidence (0.0-1.0). Only include well-known parent relationships you are confident about.

Suppliers:
{names_json}'
Use model from config.llm.model (claude-sonnet-4-20250514). Max tokens 1000. Temperature 0.
Parse JSON response, cap all confidence values at 0.50, set method='LLM_PARENT'
Log each LLM call via log_llm_call() from src/utils/logging.py
Handle API errors gracefully: log error, return None parent for affected batch
CLI: python src/suppliers/parent_mapper.py — with dry_run=true (default), prints 'DRY RUN' message for sample supplier list

userStories.title: Implement harmoniser orchestrator
userStories.description: Complete src/suppliers/harmoniser.py with the full SupplierHarmoniser orchestrator class that runs all 5 pipeline stages in order, produces the supplier_master and supplier_match_log tables, and updates the transactions table with canonical supplier IDs. This is the main entry point for the supplier harmonisation phase.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/suppliers/harmoniser.py — implement SupplierHarmoniser class (in addition to the build_supplier_master function from US-005)
__init__(self, config, engine): initialises SupplierNormaliser, DeterministicMatcher, FuzzyMatcher, EmbeddingMatcher, ParentMapper, loads config thresholds
Implement harmonise(self, transactions_df: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]: accepts transactions DataFrame (from ingestion), returns (supplier_master_df, match_log_df)

Pipeline: (1) Extract unique (raw_supplier_name, raw_supplier_id) pairs from transactions_df. (2) Normalise all names with SupplierNormaliser. (3) Group by normalised_name — rows with identical normalised_name are already the same supplier. (4) Build initial supplier_master via build_supplier_master(). (5) For each raw supplier not matched by normalisation alone, run DeterministicMatcher against existing master. (6) For remaining unmatched, run FuzzyMatcher. (7) For remaining unmatched, run EmbeddingMatcher. (8) Run ParentMapper on all canonical suppliers without a parent. (9) Write supplier_master to DB. (10) Write match_log entries for all raw→canonical mappings to DB. (11) Return both DataFrames.

Implement update_transactions(self, transactions_df: pd.DataFrame, match_log_df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame: joins match_log onto transactions by raw_supplier_name, populates canonical_supplier_id, canonical_supplier_name, parent_company_id, parent_company_name, supplier_match_confidence, supplier_match_method columns

Implement get_review_queue(self, match_log_df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame: returns rows where confidence < config.categorisation.confidence_medium (0.60), sorted by supplier spend desc (requires transactions_df join)

CLI: python src/suppliers/harmoniser.py --db data/db/spend_cube.db: loads transactions from DB, runs full harmonisation pipeline, prints summary: unique raw suppliers, canonical suppliers created, match method breakdown, review queue size

risks: sentence-transformers download on first run: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 is ~90MB. Mitigation: EmbeddingMatcher catches ImportError and returns EMBEDDING_UNAVAILABLE gracefully. Model downloads to HuggingFace cache (~/.cache/huggingface).

Fuzzy matching on small supplier master: Stage 3 fuzzy matching against a small master (10 rows) will score well. At scale (50K suppliers) this becomes O(n) per query — for v1 this is acceptable, Phase 2+ can add blocking/indexing.
Normalisation over-aggressively strips tokens: e.g. normalise('Group') → '' if 'Group' is in suffixes. Mitigation: after stripping, if result is empty string, fall back to lowercased original name.
SHA256 canonical_supplier_id collisions: extremely unlikely with 12 hex chars (48 bits). Acceptable for v1.
outOfScope: Blocking/indexing for 50K+ supplier fuzzy matching performance (v1 scale is acceptable)
